_comment: Every port is fixed, and none may be reassigned. `autoPort: true` looks harmless and
is not: on this project a moved port fails silently rather than loudly.
1. `BACKEND_PORT = 8080` is a hardcoded constant in both sites' src/lib/apiClient.ts.
`apiBase()` derives the host from wherever the page was opened but always appends
this port, so every API call goes to :8080 whatever the backend is listening on.
outright that it must match the Google console entry exactly, INCLUDING THE PORT.
A moved port cannot be fixed locally — it needs an edit in Google Cloud.
PERSONAL SITE, port 3000, and INTERNSHIPS SITE, port 3001 — CORS and redirects:
The backend's default ALLOWED_ORIGINS names exactly these two, FRONTEND_ORIGIN defaults to
3000 and HUNT_SITE_ORIGIN to 3001, and the personal site's proxy.ts sends /internships to
3001. A site that started anywhere else would have every credentialed request rejected by
the browser with no server error, so it would read as signed-out with nothing in any log.
Failing to start is strictly better than that. The personal site was `autoPort: true`
until 2026-09-05; the internships site was split out of it on 2026-11-11.
If a port is genuinely occupied, free it rather than reassigning it.
